To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CM1A charge model is superior to the CM3A charge model and to the EPS charge model, and that the CM1‐scaled charge model is superior in accuracy to the CM3‐scaled charge model, for the hydration of a diverse set of 25 organic molecules.

the CM1 and the CM3 charge models, when properly scaled, lead to hydration free energies of organic molecules in water that are comparable in accuracy to those obtained using the electrostatic potential‐based charges and that are significantly more accurate than the charges obtained from the OPLIS force field.

(i) the scaled CM1A and CM3A charges yield the lowest average errors of all the models tested and (ii) these charges yield good results for the hydration free energies of amides including a reasonable value for the E/Z free energy difference of N‐methyl acetamide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the free energy of hydration of organic molecules.
the development of methods and software for accurate and efficient calculations of the free energies of reactions in condensed phases.
the calculation of the free energy of hydration of organic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the CM3A and CM3B charges give the best overall agreement with experiment of any of the models tested here, the differences between these charges and the scaled CM1A or CM3A charges are not statistically significant.
the scaled CM1A and CM3A charges are the best available for use in free‐energy perturbation calculations.
the CM3A partial charges are the best available for the purpose of computing absolute ΔGhyds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CM1A and CM3A partial atomic charges derived using PM3 wave functions are comparable to the EPS charges derived from 6‐31+G* wave functions in terms of accuracy for the hydration free energies of 25 diverse organic solutes.
CM1 and CM2 charges are not better than the EPS charges for hydration calculations.
the best charges for the calculation of absolute hydration free energies of organic molecules are obtained from ab initio calculations of the electrostatic potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PM3‐derived CM1 and CM2 charges are not superior to EPS charges for the calculation of free energies of solvation.
the CM3 atomic charges, when scaled by 1.1, yield the lowest average errors for absolute free energies of hydration of organic molecules, compared with the CM1 charges scaled by 1/1.14.
the CM1 and the CM3 atomic charges are not as accurate as the charges fit to the ab initio electrostatic potential surface.
